body.statement:
Fix a conditional-mean interior law \(P\) in the published OVS model.  Suppose \(X\) has fixed finite support with every support mass bounded below, retained-cell overlap and the fourth-moment condition hold, and \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed.  For a declared rule \(z\in\{\mathrm{OVS},\mathrm{const}\}\), let \(b_z(P)\) be the law-dependent comparator, define \(\mu(P)\), \(F_z\), and \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}\) by Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\), and take \(\tau_n\downarrow0\) with \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n\to0\).  Let
\[
d_z=DF_z^\sharp\{\mu(P)\},
\qquad
\xi_z(O)=d_z'[U(O)-\mu(P)],
\qquad
V_{\Delta,z}=E_P[\xi_z(O)^2].
\]
If \(V_{\Delta,z}>0\), then
\[
F_z\{\mu(P)\}=\operatorname{Var}_P\{b_z(P)'\Psi_P(O)\}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P),
\tag{W1}
\]
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)\}
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_z(O_i)+o_P(1)
\ \Rightarrow\ N(0,V_{\Delta,z}),
\tag{W2}
\]
and \(\widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}\to_PV_{\Delta,z}\).  Hence the two-sided Wald interval has pointwise asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\).  If additionally \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)\ge\delta_0>0\), its lower endpoint is at least \(\delta_0/2\) with probability tending to one.  These conclusions are pointwise; they are not uniform at an equality or rank-changing boundary.
body.proof_tex:
Write the support of \(X\) as \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_D\}\).  The separate support coordinates in Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\) give
\[
 P(X=x_d)=E_P[U_d^X].
\tag{W3}
\]
For every retained cell, positivity of the support mass and retained-cell overlap make the following denominators nonzero:
\[
 p_{a,s}(x_d)
 =\frac{E_P[U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}]}{E_P[U_d^X]},
 \qquad
 m_{a,s,u}(x_d)
 =\frac{E_P[U^{(1,u)}_{d,a,s}]}{E_P[U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}]},
\tag{W4}
\]
and
\[
 E_P[\Delta Y_u\Delta Y_v\mid G=a,S=s,X=x_d]
 =\frac{E_P[U^{(2,u,v)}_{d,a,s}]}{E_P[U^{(0)}_{d,a,s}]}.
\tag{W5}
\]
Because \(D\), \(T\), and \(\mathcal G\) are finite, (W3)--(W5) reconstruct all support masses, cell probabilities, first moments, and second cross-moments.  The formulas in the core then reconstruct \(\pi\), \(q\), \(\theta\), \(\Psi\), \(\Omega\), \(Z^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), \(K_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), and \(r_{\mathrm{OVS}}\) as explicit functions of \(\mu(P)\).

The corrected score vector has mean zero.  Therefore the variance of the declared law-dependent comparator is
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P\{b_z(P)'\Psi_P\}
 =b_z\{\mu(P)\}'\Omega\{\mu(P)\}b_z\{\mu(P)\}.
\tag{W6}
\]
Let \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}\) be the reference loading from Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\).  Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\) and finite-support conditioning give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
 &=E_P[(\psi_P^0)^2]
 -E_P[r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger
 r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)]\\
 &=b^{\mathrm{ref}\prime}\Omega\{\mu(P)\}b^{\mathrm{ref}}
 -\sum_{d=1}^D P(X=x_d)
 r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d)^\dagger
 r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{W7}
\]
Subtracting (W7) from (W6) is exactly formula (G4) defining \(F_z\).  This proves
\[
 F_z\{\mu(P)\}
 =\operatorname{Var}_P\{b_z(P)'\Psi_P\}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
 =\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P).
\tag{W8}
\]
In particular, the reconstruction differentiates the rule \(P\mapsto b_z(P)\); it does not incorrectly hold a numerical loading fixed while differentiating the law.

We next establish the stochastic order required by the selected-rank lemma.  The fourth-moment assumption and
\[
 |\Delta Y_u|^4\le 8(|Y_u|^4+|Y_{u-1}|^4),
 \qquad
 (\Delta Y_u\Delta Y_v)^2
 \le\frac12\{(\Delta Y_u)^4+(\Delta Y_v)^4\}
\tag{W9}
\]
show that every coordinate of \(U(O)\) has a finite second moment.  Coordinatewise Chebyshev inequalities, combined over the fixed dimension \(d_\mu\), yield
\[
 \widehat\mu-\mu(P)=O_P(n^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \Sigma_U:=\operatorname{Var}_P\{U(O)\}<\infty.
\tag{W10}
\]

At the fixed law, there are only finitely many matrices \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(x_d)\) and comparator KKT matrices.  Each is real symmetric, and the minimum absolute value among all of their nonzero eigenvalues is strictly positive.  On the overlap domain their entries are continuously differentiable rational functions of \(\mu\); all ordinary denominators are nonzero by (W3)--(W5).  Lemma \(\ref{lem:fixed-support-selected-rank-delta}\), applied with \(z=\mu\), (W10), \(\tau_n\downarrow0\), and \(n^{-1/2}/\tau_n\to0\), therefore proves simultaneous population-rank recovery and
\[
 F_{z,\tau_n}(\widehat\mu)-F_z\{\mu(P)\}
 =d_z'\{\widehat\mu-\mu(P)\}+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{W11}
\]
Since \(\widehat\mu-\mu(P)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n[U(O_i)-\mu(P)]\), equations (W8) and (W11) give
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)\}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_z(O_i)+o_P(1).
\tag{W12}
\]
The summands are independent and identically distributed by the sampling assumption, have mean zero by definition, and have variance \(V_{\Delta,z}\in(0,\infty)\) by (W10) and the stated positivity condition.  Lemma \(\ref{lem:iid-central-limit}\), followed by the elementary fact that adding an \(o_P(1)\) term preserves convergence at every continuity point, proves the normal limit in (W2).

It remains to prove variance consistency under the stated moments.  Rank recovery and continuity of the selected branch imply
\[
 \widehat d_z\longrightarrow_P d_z.
\tag{W13}
\]
For any entry \(W=U_jU_k\), \(E_P|W|<\infty\) by Cauchy--Schwarz and (W10).  Let \(W_M=W\mathbf 1\{|W|\le M\}\).  The sample average of bounded \(W_M\) converges in probability to its expectation by Chebyshev's inequality, while Markov's inequality gives, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 P\{\mathbb P_n|W-W_M|>\epsilon\}
 \le \epsilon^{-1}E_P[|W|\mathbf 1\{|W|>M\}].
\tag{W14}
\]
The right side tends to zero as \(M\to\infty\).  Finiteness of the matrix dimension and \(\widehat\mu\to_P\mu(P)\) consequently imply
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
 \{U(O_i)-\widehat\mu\}\{U(O_i)-\widehat\mu\}'
 \longrightarrow_P\Sigma_U.
\tag{W15}
\]
Premultiplying and postmultiplying (W15) by \(\widehat d_z\), and using (W13), gives
\[
 \widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}
 \longrightarrow_P d_z'\Sigma_Ud_z=V_{\Delta,z}.
\tag{W16}
\]

Let \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) be the \((1-\alpha/2)\)-quantile of the standard normal law.  Equations (W12) and (W16), with \(V_{\Delta,z}>0\), imply
\[
 T_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}\Rightarrow N(0,1),
\]
so the interval
\[
 \left[\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}
 -z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}/n},\ 
 \widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}
 +z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}/n}\right]
\]
has pointwise limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\).  Finally, (W12) gives \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)=O_P(n^{-1/2})\), and (W16) makes the half-width \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\).  If \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},z}(P)\ge\delta_0>0\), their sum in absolute value is below \(\delta_0/2\) with probability tending to one.  The lower endpoint is then at least \(\delta_0/2\), as claimed.  The argument fixes the law and its selected ranks throughout, so it makes no uniform assertion at an equality or rank-changing boundary.
body.justification: The explicit moment map closes pointwise inference for the published-bound gap in the certified finite-support regime.
body.gap: The theorem is separated from equality and rank-changing boundaries and does not claim uniform coverage there.
body.consumer: The backend may expose a gap estimate, plug-in standard error, and Wald interval when its fixed-support checks pass.
